summary: Join specialized training on Public-Private Partnerships in Social Protection. Learn strategies to effectively collaborate for social impact and sustainability.
lede: Public-private partnership training in social protection covers how to identify suitable opportunities and design arrangements around program goals. It is for government, NGO, development, and private-sector professionals who plan, negotiate, finance, implement, or oversee these partnerships. Participants learn to map stakeholders and incentives, allocate risks, structure agreements and performance measures, assess payment models, protect beneficiaries, and use monitoring evidence to improve partnerships.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals involved in designing, negotiating, financing, implementing, or regulating PPPs in social protection. This course is designed for: Government officials responsible for social protection policy and program implementation. PPP unit staff working on social sector projects. Managers in ministries of finance, social welfare, labor, health, or education. NGO and INGO leaders partnering with governments or private firms to deliver services. Representatives from private companies, social enterprises, and insurers engaged in social protection schemes. Development partner staff involved in funding or advising PPPs in social protection. Social protection program managers overseeing cash transfers, social insurance, or safety net schemes. Procurement and contract management professionals managing service delivery agreements. Regulators overseeing service quality, data protection, and beneficiary safeguards. Strategy and planning professionals designing multi-stakeholder initiatives in social protection.
modules: Foundations of Public-Private Partnerships in Social Protection
Social Protection Systems and Entry Points for PPPs
Stakeholder Mapping, Incentives, and Partnership Models
Risk Identification and Allocation in Social Protection PPPs
Financing, Payment Models, and Value for Money
Case Studies of PPPs in Social Protection
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning in Social Protection PPPs
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of social protection systems and some experience in project management or policy development. Familiarity with public-private partnership concepts is beneficial but not required.
